summary.headline: Websol Q1 FY27 revenue rose 70% YoY to INR373 crore and PAT grew 16% to INR78 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 34% from 47% on module mix.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR373 crore, up 70% YoY and down about 7% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR126 crore (+21% YoY, margin 34% vs 47%) and PAT of INR78 crore (+16%). Cell output rose to 259 MW (92% utilisation) and module output to 103 MW (81% utilisation), with module volume doubling and driving the margin dilution. The company repaid the INR110 crore IREDA term loan on 4 August from internal accruals, with promoter pledge set to fall from 80% to 16% of promoter holding once released. Phase 3 expansion is being relocated from Andhra Pradesh to West Bengal, with land approval awaited; management says capex, cost and timelines are unchanged.

segments.name: Solar cells
segments.commentary: Production 259 MW vs 126 MW in Q1 FY26, utilisation 92%; average cell efficiency 23.3%. About 153 MW sold externally in Q1, with the rest consumed captively for modules.

segments.name: Solar modules
segments.commentary: Production 103 MW vs 50 MW, utilisation 81% vs 39%. Module margins are lower than cell margins, and module-led mix is the main driver of the margin decline.

guidance_outlook: Cell utilisation of about 92% to be held; management expects close to full run-rate utilisation across lines except TOPCon upgrade downtime.

TOPCon upgrade of 600 MW mono PERC line to 750 MW TOPCon, lifting total cell capacity to 1.3 GW (about 55% TOPCon), expected by March 2027 at about INR270 crore, funded from internal accruals with possible debt.
Management expects payback of 2 to 3 years on the TOPCon capex; cell efficiency expected around 25% post-upgrade.

Phase 3 (4 GW total, cell and module, two phases of 2 GW each): land approval expected in August; construction targeted mid-September; equipment lead time 4 to 6 months; trial run after about 2 months post installation; management says no change in timelines or capex.
Margins: management expects cell margins to fall somewhat but not aggressively, and believes current margin levels can hold for a year or two.
Silver consumption cut 20% in FY26, with a further 10% reduction target for cells.
capex_capacity: Current capacity: cells about 1.2 GW pre-upgrade, rising to 1.35 GW (per management, with 750 MW TOPCon) after the TOPCon upgrade; the upgrade adds about 150 MW of cell capacity.

Phase 3: 4 GW of additional cell and 4 GW of module capacity in two 2 GW phases; location moved from Andhra Pradesh (Naidupeta) to West Bengal (land shortlisted near Falta facility, approval pending).
Expected timeline: land approval in August 2026, construction from mid-September, equipment ordered around December, arrival April to May 2027, about 9 months to complete, then 2 months of trials.
Module utilisation of 81% described as close to full effective utilisation; industry comfort range cited at 70-75%.
demand_pricing: Prices softened in the previous quarter; management says prices rose in the current quarter on ALMM-related expectations, but the ALMM cell mandate was deferred from June to December 2026.
Current cell price quoted at about USD0.13 per Wp and module at about INR21 per watt, against Q1 levels of about USD0.125 and INR20.50.

Demand is mainly DCR (PM-Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM); management sees no decline. Inventory rose about 7% QoQ and management attributes it to monsoon-season offtake slowdown and captive cell blocking in modules.
Input costs: silver prices have eased but imported paste carries a lag; wafer prices are flat. The West Asia conflict has raised BOM costs for modules, not cells.
Management said Q1 margin decline reflects lower cell prices and higher silver and BOM cost, alongside mix shift.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company moving Phase 3 from Andhra Pradesh to West Bengal, and does it change timelines and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited synergies in skilled manpower, supply chain and infrastructure, with no change to capex, project cost, funding or timelines; no financial outflow had occurred on the AP land.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin trend and is margin pressure expected to persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to module-heavy mix plus lower cell prices and higher silver/BOM costs; it expects cell margins to fall but not aggressively and to hold current levels for a year or two.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory rising, and what were Q1 realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose about 7% QoQ, which management attributed to monsoon-led offtake slowdown and cell cost blocked in modules; Q1 realisations were about USD0.125/Wp for cells and INR20.50/W for modules.

qa_highlights.question: What returns does the TOPCon upgrade generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects incremental revenue from higher Wp per cell (7.6-7.7 Wp for PERC to about 9.5 Wp for TOPCon), higher capacity (600 MW to 750 MW) and a price premium; it expects a 2-3 year payback on the INR270 crore capex.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company targeting a larger order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order book reports only firm purchase orders and repeat business, and the company is not targeting a higher order book; it sees regular DCR-market inquiries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ability to execute and ramp Phase 3 at the same pace?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the TOPCon conversion will serve as practical training before the greenfield expansion; it cited the mono PERC installation timeline as precedent.

risks_watch: Margin compression as module mix rises: EBITDA margin fell 13 percentage points YoY to 34%, and management expects further cell margin softening.
Phase 3 execution: relocation to West Bengal depends on pending land approval (targeted August 2026); no incentive terms disclosed yet.
Inventory build (about 7% QoQ) and monsoon-season offtake; watch whether it clears in Q2.
ALMM cell mandate deferred to December 2026 and dependence on domestic cell capacity; price direction after that date.
Investor-communication concerns raised by several participants (valuation, share-price moves, lack of disclosure). The company said it is increasing investor interactions.
Pledge release: promoter pledge reduction from 80% to 16% depends on lender formalities; timing unconfirmed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and utilisation and on the debt repayment, but defensive and vague on valuation, share price, Phase 3 incentives and cost savings, where it declined to give figures and said it would disclose later.

key_quotes: We did this without raising fresh capital and without slowing any of our ongoing growth investments.
In absolute terms, EBITDA still grew 21% because additional module volume adds to earning even as it reduces the percentage margin.
Whatever capacity we have announced is what we are confident of executing.
So, we expect the payback between 2 to 3 years of this capex expansion.
